fix(proc): a refusal is a child still running at the escalation (candybar-testing-0x6u.0mz)

A pid probe cannot classify a group's EPERM: it missed a zombie left behind a
reaped leader. The launch owns its child's end, so SIGKILL's answer decides.
fix(proc): a zombie child's group is no refusal of its signal (candybar-testing-0x6u.0mz)

feat(daemon): close says when the launches it ended have ended (candybar-testing-0x6u.keo) (#532)

* feat(daemon): close says when the launches it ended have ended (candybar-testing-0x6u.keo)

* fix(daemon): settled holds the loop, and its tests wait on the child they mean (candybar-testing-0x6u.keo)

* fix(proc): unreaped reads the child's own end, and a lost lifeline holds the loop too (candybar-testing-0x6u.keo)

* fix(proc): the pipes of a killed launch go after its end, with its output read (candybar-testing-0x6u.keo)

* test(proc): the busy-loop case blocks where timers run next (candybar-testing-0x6u.keo)

* fix(proc): setImmediate comes from node:timers (candybar-testing-0x6u.keo)

## [1.173.1](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/compare/v1.173.0...v1.173.1) (2026-11-01)

### Bug Fixes

* **test:** a fake launch holds the run, and the daemon test keeps only the wiring (brandon-unfiled-3248.2ywj) ([#531](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/issues/531)) ([7b77d5f](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/commit/7b77d5fab04cc3822fa430e086169ef7f984b873))

fix(test): a render's event records the wait it armed, and the deadline case reads that (brandon-unfiled-3248.a5k3)

The case asserted Date.now() <= deadline right after the reply, which
times the test worker's loop: on PR #474's CI it read 47 ms past. The
unstated branch made the same comparison against a tighter bound.

RequestWait carried one fact twice, `ms` for the event and `endsAt` for
the timer, so `deadline=` could disagree with the wait that ran. `ms` is
gone, and the event notes the value `waitWithin` is armed with.

The case now reads that figure and its bound, with no clock read after
the reply. Nothing left about it is the process's, so it moves back to
the worker. `/^stated:\d+ms$/` is gone with it: a request read late
records a negative budget, and that regex refused it.

test/wait-within.test.ts gains the case that times when a wait ends. The
existing ones said only which arm ended it.
